headline: Highest risk is medium: shared filesystem and permissive tool-use create prompt-injection and data-leak pathways, but no direct destructive default action is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP, while Superset exposes an API surface; if Continue ingests Superset-generated content or shared files as instructions, prompt injection is plausible. The pair shares state via filesystem, so interaction is not isolated. No evidence shows a stronger shared channel, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF Continue reads Superset-produced files or API responses as trusted instructions
IF both agents share the same workspace directory without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from shared files
Separate workspaces per agent
Add provenance labels to files exchanged between agents
Require manual review before MCP tool calls
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization/provenance filters

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and can write/read the filesystem; Superset has an API surface and allowlisted egress. If sensitive code or buffers are shared into Superset workflows, data can flow beyond the editor boundary. The profiles do not prove uncontrolled exfiltration, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace
IF Continue forwards file contents into Superset-accessible workflows or outputs
mitigations: Restrict shared folders to non-sensitive projects
Turn off automatic file attachment in Continue
Use separate OS accounts for each agent
Review Superset API access paths before enabling them
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on workspace reads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Superset has API access and allowlisted network egress. Even without explicit git writes, both can mutate shared resources through the filesystem or APIs, creating overlapping-write risk. Because the exact shared mutable target is not documented, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same writable directory
IF Superset API actions and Continue file edits target the same project state
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent
Pause one agent during bulk edits by the other
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Limit Continue to read-only mode on shared repos
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or facts from editor buffers, and Superset can consume API-driven workflows or present downstream analytics. If Superset treats Continue output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect analytics or actions. The profiles do not show direct autonomous action-taking, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Superset consumes Continue output without a verification step
IF generated code or facts are copied from Continue into Superset workflows
mitigations: Require human verification before reuse of Continue output
Add checksum or citation checks on transferred artifacts
Keep Continue output in draft-only channels
Document a review step in the workflow
requires-engineering: build validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and no PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented. Continue handles model-provider API keys and workspace content, while Superset lists no sensitive data classes. With no evidence of regulated-data flow, compliance risk is limited and lower than the interaction risks.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into the shared workspace
IF either deployment is configured with stricter residency or retention rules than the other
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workspaces
Confirm retention settings for any connected model provider
Document data-class boundaries for each agent
Use separate environments for regulated projects
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
